subject.title: [Feature]: Add JSON-RPC bindings for language-agnostic plugins

question: Should OpenClaw accept the JSON-RPC manifest/plugin SDK ABI proposed in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/98005 as a supported plugin-author contract, narrow or gate it, or defer language-neutral plugin bindings for now?
rationale: The missing capability is real, but accepting it freezes new public SDK, manifest, child-process lifecycle, compatibility, security, and support semantics that automation should not decide.

options.title: Accept protocol v1 after owner review
options.body: Review the linked PR's ABI, host-permission model, lifecycle limits, docs, and proof, then land it as the supported implementation if the contract is acceptable.

options.title: Narrow or gate the ABI
options.body: Keep the issue open while reducing the supported registration forms, marking the bridge experimental, or adding stricter capability gates before release.

options.title: Defer language-neutral bindings
options.body: Close or pause the implementation PR and keep this issue as a design record if maintainers are not ready to own a child-process plugin ABI.

recommendation.title: Accept protocol v1 after owner review
recommendation.body: Review the linked PR's ABI, host-permission model, lifecycle limits, docs, and proof, then land it as the supported implementation if the contract is acceptable.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is about the public plugin SDK boundary and plugin architecture direction, where history points to steipete as the original architecture and adjacent SDK/docs contributor.
